Booking Holdings is bringing together two of its business-to-business travel operations in a new division it hopes will be transformational, betting that a larger, coordinated partner platform can generate growth as artificial intelligence changes how travelers discover and book trips.

The fresh enterprise unit, dubbed Booking Partner Division, will combine Booking.com Strategic Partnerships with Rocket Travel by Agoda, and is set to begin operating in January. Agoda CEO Omri Morgenshtern will lead the unit, which aims to help businesses such as banks, airlines and online travel companies sell trips or build branded experiences for their customers.

"We realize that if we focus our efforts both on the product side, but also on the go-to-market side, then we can potentially grow faster and serve better partners," Morgenshtern told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

He remarked existing partners will find fresh and better products, which will also help grow the partner base.

The move gives Booking a single organization to coordinate technology, travel supply and commercial expertise across business relationships. The tech giant says partners will be able to use its global supply and technology through white-label platforms, integrated applications, branded solutions and hotel-chain rate distribution.

The portfolio includes more than 4.7 million properties, 33 million accommodation listings, more than 500 airlines and more than 200 car rental providers, according to the tech giant.

Competitor Expedia Group has seen notable growth by prioritizing its enterprise efforts, including a strategy rolled out in 2022 to make its technology platform available to business partners looking to add travel to their own offerings.

From 2018 to 2023, Expedia’s business-to-business revenue grew at a 16% compound annual rate, while adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or EBITDA, for the division grew at a 28% rate, the firm mentioned in 2024.

In a recent development, in 2025, Expedia’s B2B revenue rose 18% to $4.8 billion, and its segment adjusted EBITDA increased 22% to $1.26 billion. Those figures represented about a third of Expedia’s total revenue and more than a third of its adjusted EBITDA for the full year.

Morgenshtern declined to say how much the fresh division is expected to contribute to Booking Holdings' overall revenue and profit, but he said the opportunity for growth is immense, estimating the total addressable market at $2 trillion.

Online travel agencies have been pressured this year as investors scrutinize how AI will change the way customers search for and then book their travel.

Companies that offer lodging, experiences and other travel and leisure are grappling with how to stay visible if AI tools become the upcoming starting point for planning and reservations.

Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro said on the tech giant’s earnings call Tuesday that guests already use AI to discover and proposal Disney trips, and that some are using the tools to book.

“Ultimately, we want Disney to show up in those tools,” he mentioned, adding that Disney is exploring ways to let guests make reservations directly from them.

Booking anticipates offering partners AI capabilities that draw on the tech giant's existing travel know-how while minimizing token costs, it stated.

"I see a lot of AI demos," Morgenshtern remarked, drawing a distinction between a product that caters to a few customers and one that's scalable and works even when overloaded by travel emergencies. He said he's "super optimistic" about the bespoke product — a vertical agent — that Booking will offer to its partners.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an upgrade today (in Mandarin; translation by Google).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station.

According to recent reports, that pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft early this morning (Nov. 25).

"The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an upgrade today (in Mandarin; translation by Google). "China's 'Tiangong' welcomes partners from all over the world to visit!".

Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, is a payload specialist on Shenzhou-24. He found his way onto the mission thanks to a space-cooperation agreement that China signed with Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025.

Industry observers note that ali and his two Shenzhou-24 crewmates — commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi — enjoyed a short and smooth ride to their orbital destination. They lifted off atop a Long March 2F rocket on Tuesday (Nov. 24) at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT on Nov. 25) and reached Tiangong a little over six hours later.

Tang and Wu will live aboard the outpost for the usual six-month stint. Ali, however, will come home in just a week, hitching a ride with two of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong in May.

Ali will be busy during his short space stay, conducting a set of joint Chinese-Pakistani experiments.

"Four collaborative projects in biotechnology and materials are planned, with Ali also scheduled to conduct an in-orbit experiment involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria," The Times of India wrote today.

The third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will remain on the station until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore set a Chinese record, becoming the first astronaut from his country to live in low Earth orbit for a full year.

Sources indicate that astronauts from the Soviet Union/Russia and the United States have already blazed this long-duration trail. The global record for longest continuous space stay is 437 days, set by cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov aboard the Mir space station from January 1994 to March 1995.

Industry observers note that ali is not the first person from Pakistan ever to reach space, by the way. That distinction belongs to adventurer Namira Salim, who traveled to suborbital space on a tourism flight with Virgin Galactic in October 2023.

Shenzhou-24 is the 12th crewed mission to Tiangong, a three-module, T-shaped outpost that China finished assembling in late 2022. Well, "finished" might not be the right term; China plans to expand Tiangong, which is right now about 20% as massive as the International Space Station.

Sean “Diddy” Combs isn’t skipping out on Turkey Day.

Sources indicate that after all, the rapper—who is serving a 50-month prison sentence for prostitution related charges at FCI Allenwood Low in Pennsylvania—will enjoy a full-course meal come Nov. 26, a law enforcement official at the prison confirmed to People.

Combs' Thanksgiving menu includes a choice between turkey and tofu stir-fry, they told the outlet, along with sides like mashed potatoes and candied sweet potato casserole.

And it appears the music mogul will be able to enjoy all the fixings as the menu also features green bean casserole, sage and onion stuffing and dinner rolls, the official confirmed. Combs will also have his choice of gravy and cranberry sauce for the meal.

According to recent reports, and what’s Thanksgiving without dessert? This year, the 57-year-old will satisfy his sweet tooth with pecan pie.

Industry observers note that E! News has reached out to Combs’ rep for comment but did not hear back.

But not every inmate will be getting the same spread. In fact, the Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) does not offer a standardized holiday menu across all facilities. Rather, some have more flexibility with their menus than others.

Industry observers note that holiday meals “reflect available food items, local considerations, and the cultural diversity of the inmate population,” a spokesperson told Oxygen. “This allows institutions to incorporate menu enhancements and provide meals that recognize the specific holiday.”.

The statement added, “The same goes for any planned activities at each facility.”.

Though this Thanksgiving marks Combs’ third behind bars, it’s his first at FCI Allenwood Low, where he was transferred in October after sustaining a head injury while incarcerated at Upcoming Jersey's FCI Fort Dix.

"His transfer from one low-security facility to another is an important distinction, and while we cannot speak to the BOP's specific reasons for the move, it is consistent with a decision made with safety and security in mind,” Combs’ rep told E! in an Oct. 16 statement. "We are grateful for the attention being given to his well-being and hope he can continue serving his time without unnecessary disruption.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The location and the gesture were carefully chosen: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stood side by side, laid flowers and bowed their heads at the military cemetery in the center of the Ukrainian city of Uzhhorod.
  • One of those buried there is an ethnic Hungarian who was one of the first soldiers killed in Russia's full-scale war of aggression against Ukraine.
  • Magyar intentionally chose not to begin his first visit to Ukraine as prime minister at a government building.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The location and the gesture were carefully chosen: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stood side by side, laid flowers and bowed their heads at the military cemetery in the center of the Ukrainian city of Uzhhorod.

One of those buried there is an ethnic Hungarian who was one of the first soldiers killed in Russia's full-scale war of aggression against Ukraine.

Magyar intentionally chose not to begin his first visit to Ukraine as prime minister at a government building. Instead, his Tuesday afternoon visit began at a place where he could demonstrate his solidarity with Ukraine more clearly than anywhere else.

Uzhhorod, known as Ungvar in Hungarian, is the capital of Ukraine's Transcarpathia region, which is home to around 80,000 members of Ukraine's Hungarian minority. Thousands of ethnic Hungarians are fighting Russian occupying forces on the front lines.

For Hungary, where ethnic Hungarian minorities in neighboring countries traditionally play an notable role, the war is therefore closer to home than it is for other European countries.

In a recent development, magyar described his visit to Ukraine as a "historic day" in a Facebook post. Before the ceremony at the cemetery in Uzhhorod, he said: "I bring with me the solidarity of the Hungarian people. We stand with Ukraine against the Russian aggressor.".

Zelenskyy responded on X, saying "We appreciate this gesture of respect toward those who sacrificed their lives for Ukraine's independence.".

The meeting between Magyar and Zelenskyy marked a turning point in Hungary's approach to Ukraine.

In a recent development, the two leaders repeatedly shook hands throughout the day. Such scenes would have been unthinkable just a few months ago. The propaganda of Magyar's pro-Russian predecessor, Viktor Orban, portrayed Ukraine as a "mafia state" and "lawless country" on an almost daily basis.

Under Orban, relations between Hungary and Ukraine reached a historic low.

Now the two countries are seeking a political reset, which is vital not only for Hungary and Ukraine but for Europe as a whole. After all, Orban's repeated obstruction of support for Ukraine drove the EU to the brink of despair.

During talks in Uzhhorod, the two leaders also agreed to closer economic cooperation.

The talks centered on Hungarian diesel supplies to Ukraine, greater use of Ukrainian gas storage facilities by Hungarian companies, and joint infrastructure projects, including the opening of new border crossings and a direct rail link between Budapest and Kyiv.

Nevertheless, no formal agreements were signed on Tuesday.

At a subsequent news conference, journalists asked questions about sensitive issues between the two countries: minority rights, Ukraine's EU integration and a new EU loan for Ukraine.

Throughout the day, the two men were visibly keen to avoid any discord.

Magyar, for example, described his angry outburst over Ukraine's "Carpathian Eight" initiative in parliament in late September as a "misunderstanding" and suggested that Hungary might, after all, take part.

Zelenskyy's cautious replies to journalists suggest that he knows his country's path to EU membership also runs through Budapest.

One of Magyar's statements on Tuesday was key: "We've finally put a stop to this completely unnecessary and inexplicable political escalation.".

In a recent development, even before taking office in early May 2026, Magyar had promised to reset relations with Ukraine. But the process has not been entirely smooth.

Sources indicate that in many respects — but certainly not all — Magyar is distancing himself from his predecessor. He has made no bones of the fact that he sees Russia as the aggressor, but he rejects both arms deliveries to Ukraine and even the transit of weapons across Hungarian territory.

Magyar previously accused Ukraine of treating ethnic Hungarians as second-class citizens — a claim that is not borne out by the facts. He pressed for greater minority rights and for a time blocked the opening of negotiating chapters in Ukraine's EU accession talks.

Magyar also departed from diplomatic convention by choosing the location of his meeting with Zelenskyy in Ukraine: Indeed, it was Magyar who invited Zelenskyy to Transcarpathia.

Magyar's sometimes confrontational tone toward Ukraine can also be explained by the need to avoid appearing too pro-Ukrainian to the Hungarian public.

Sources indicate that according to a November 2026 poll conducted by the think tank Globsec, 33% of Hungarians would now support their country providing military aid to Ukraine. Although this is much more than during Orban's time in office, many Hungarians remain skeptical of Ukraine.

That's why Olena Halushka, a Ukrainian political scientist at the International Centre for Ukrainian Victory (ICUV), sees some aspects of Magyar's visit as a concession to public opinion in Hungary.

It has been revealed that "Magyar has taken over a deeply polarized country," she told DW's Ukrainian Service. "A visit to Transcarpathia is more of a step for the Hungarian population than for Ukraine.".

Ukraine accommodated not only Magyar's choice of location but also Hungary's demands for better protection of minority rights, which were set out in a 10-point blueprint in June. That's because EU integration is one of the country's top political priorities.

After planned restrictions on the use of minority languages were withdrawn in late 2023, Ukraine's parliament in early October passed a law on minority language rights that in some respects goes even further than European standards.

Hungary subsequently dropped its obstruction of the opening of negotiating clusters for Ukraine's EU accession.

Laszlo Zubanics, chairman of the Hungarian Democratic Federation in Ukraine (UMDSZ, one of two Hungarian political parties in Transcarpathia), told DW that the Magyar-Zelenskyy meeting was "historic.".

He particularly welcomed the fact that Ukraine will probably implement practical improvements in the protection of minority rights "not only by the end of 2027, but much sooner, within just a few months.".

A Hungarian diplomat who spoke to DW on condition of anonymity also called the meeting "historic," adding that after the Orban government's anti-Ukrainian policies, trust now needs to be rebuilt, and that personal meetings between the two leaders play an key role in that process.

The diplomat went on to say that Hungary not only wants to ensure that the rights of the Hungarian minority are protected, it also has a strong interest in being involved in Ukraine's reconstruction.

Overall, the diplomat concluded, both sides are very keen to expand economic cooperation.

Hungarian political scientist Daniel Hegedus of the Institute for European Politics (IEP) in Berlin told DW that while the meeting was a "symbolic milestone," it will be crucial to see "how the two political leaders capitalize on the symbolic political capital generated by this meeting.".

No observers have suggested that this is the grand finale of reconciliation between Hungary and Ukraine.

Nevertheless, Tuesday's reset sends an vital signal to Europe, namely that if the political will is there, a deep gulf that has existed for years can be transformed into a set of diverging interests that can be addressed through negotiations.

Or, as Zelenskyy put it, now there are "all the opportunities to build hopefully constructive relations.".

This article was originally written in German.

Unai Emery wanted the winger but, like Harvey Elliott last season, he has been left out in the cold despite Villa’s attacking struggles.

It is three years this week since Alejandro Garnacho opened the scoring for Manchester United in a 3-3 draw at Galatasaray in the Champions League, on a typically boisterous night in Istanbul when Victor Lindelöf and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, now his teammates at Aston Villa, were also among the starters. At the time, Garnacho was a teenage star flourishing on the grandest of stages, a fixture in the United team and fresh from scoring an outrageous overhead kick at Goodison Park a few days earlier that would later clinch the Premier League’s goal-of-the-season award.

It has been revealed that he went on to score twice at Old Trafford on Boxing Day, in a 3-2 victory against Villa, and a couple of months later his double at home to West Ham was the catalyst for that iconic celebration photo of Garnacho, Kobbie Mainoo and Rasmus Højlund sitting on the advertising hoardings at the Stretford End, beaming smiles all round. All three were at the heart of United’s prepares for a bright future, beacons of hope. At the end of that season, Garnacho signed off in style, he and Mainoo scoring against Manchester City at Wembley to win the FA Cup.

Tech Report: The local boy aiming to be at the heart of Cardiff's derby aims

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Colwill has one goal and three assists from 10 Championship appearances following Cardiff City's return to the Championship.
  • Rubin Colwill is used to being in the centre of things.
  • He has been the focus of an ongoing argument over his role - or lack of it - in Craig Bellamy's Wales side.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Colwill has one goal and three assists from 10 Championship appearances following Cardiff City's return to the Championship.

Rubin Colwill is used to being in the centre of things.

He has been the focus of an ongoing argument over his role - or lack of it - in Craig Bellamy's Wales side.

It has meant the midfielder has been the subject of countless questions around international weeks, the latest prompting the Wales boss to ask a journalist if he had a Colwill poster in the middle of his bedroom wall.

The debate has stemmed from the 24-year-old being at the heart of Brian Barry-Murphy's stylish transformation of Cardiff City.

So it is understandable that, as he prepares to lead his boyhood club into the eye of the storm that is the south Wales derby, he is again in the centre of things.

And fitting for someone who grew up in the middle of the rivalry between the two cities.

"I took a lot of stick," Colwill said. Well, we presume that is what he might have said, stopping himself from swearing to describe life as a Cardiff fan from the town of Neath, nine miles from Swansea.

"I probably felt it more than most being surrounded by Swansea fans and a lot of mates being Swansea fans.

"It was tough because they were in the Premier League for a long spell, so I was always trying to give a bit back when we won a game or did well.".

Bellamy an influence as Williams leads Swansea.

Bellamy jokes reporter has Colwill poster in bedroom.

Latest Cardiff City news, analysis and fan views.

Colwill was always Cardiff, as was brother Joel, his team-mate for club and country.

Their mother - from Port Talbot, a little further east with a denser amount of support that turn towards the capital - was a Cardiff fan and so were her boys, signing for the club while still in primary school.

He has never gone to a derby in Swansea as a fan - he was never allowed - but was part of the Cardiff side that last won at their rivals in 2021 and has told team-mates all about the journey down the M4, where fans flock to bridges and encouragement turns to abuse as the miles clock up.

He will mention that, and the feeling of the times where, by his own admission, Cardiff were not good enough in a string of defeats that sting more than most.

But he will also share the "no better" feeling of being in the middle of the celebrations of a derby win, as he was in January 2025.

Colwill: 'Tough' growing up as a Cardiff fan.

That Cardiff 3-0 victory was a rare high point in a season that eventually saw the club relegated from the Championship and in desperate need of a rebuild.

They have done just that, transitioning into an eye-catching, exciting team, who - depsite failing to win away this season and going into the game on the back of a 4-0 defeat by Preston North End - are ready to show Swansea the Bluebirds are a different beast these days.

Colwill and his influence has been very much a central cog in that change.

He has been game time and responsibility by Barry-Murphy - including the armband that might not be obvious for such a seemingly laidback character.

The academy product states he has learned much from the journey, including a frustrating spell of injuries that have limited his impact to seven starts since the return to the Championship.

It has seemingly been noticed by Bellamy, who spoke before Wales' recent Nations League defeat to Portugal about how he has improved as a player.

"There has been a substantial change in his game," Bellamy remarked, a former academy coach of the talented midfielder.

"He is a player I really like watching - before I did and I didn't. Now I see a lot of good things.".

Colwill responded with a man-of-the-match performance against Portugal in what was his first competitive Wales start in five years.

"It was almost like I got to experience my first game twice," smiled Colwill.

Bellamy - who has questioned Colwill's work off the ball - has said he felt able to be more "ruthless" with the youngster because of their long association.

Industry observers note that "Everyone knows," mentioned Bellamy of what he thought Colwill needed to do to improve. "And none more than him.".

Williams to lead Swansea in south Wales derby.

Frozen out Robinson told he has Cardiff future.

Despite being in the middle of it all, Colwill has not changed in playing personality, and certainly showed no pressure when he reclaimed his Wales spot.

Clearly there is a resilience that goes beyond sticking with a Cardiff scarf in an area full of Swansea colours.

"I've tried to learn from those experiences and develop myself mentally and improve my resilience so I can almost take anything that comes my way," he says.

"I think that's a massive part of football: you've got to stay grounded, stay focused, regardless if you're doing really well or really badly because it's a massive part of the game to stay consistent in the end.".

So what of the challenge to improve and being in the middle of the two different approaches to getting the most out of him?

Recent findings suggest that "I think they're very similar," is Colwill's response. "They both want to control the game, the structure, the body shape, how they want us to play, the press and reaction to giving the ball away.

"In the fundamentals of the game, they're similar. Obviously they're both different people so the approaches to that are very different, and it's in the little details.

"With Craig, he's always had that approach of if he thinks you can offer something or improve on, it's on us to take it on board and be open to that constructive criticism.

Sources indicate that "It's not always easy. I think he does have a high demand of you, but if you do make a change as he asks of you then he will play you.".

Cardiff players will have 'edge' against Swansea.

After the stick, the carrot at Cardiff is the chance to follow in Bellamy's footsteps by scoring a winner in the derby at Swansea, as the Wales boss did in 2011 - Cardiff's last win there in front of travelling supporters.

Colwill smiles at the thought, just as he winces at the memories of the defeats - as a player and a fan - which is why he will not be telling team-mates to treat this game like just another.

"That attitude is almost like trying to protect yourself from the pressure," he argues. "But it's not. We have a lot of boys from the area who have come from the academy who really get the game and understand the whole picture of it and how key it is for everyone in the city.

"And we've got no fear of failure - if we lose we just leave it all out there, but we have full belief we can win.".

If they do, it will come as no surprise if Colwill is at the heart of it.
